locator: I q.2 a.3 co., quarta via: Invenitur enim in rebus aliquid magis et minus bonum, et verum, et nobile
interpretation: An observation premise, like the prima via's sensu constat: comparatives of goodness, truth and nobility hold between things. Only the three named perfections are asserted; 'et sic de aliis huiusmodi' is left unformalized. 'Verum' is read as ontological truth (a thing's being true), the sense the next sentence needs ('quae sunt maxime vera, sunt maxime entia').
